TARGET.statement: evidence establishing one property of a control must not automatically be treated as establishing another property required by the current decision
TARGET.sourceEvidence: §177 raw output on the frozen HR-04 row: the model quoted the control as being in position, reasoned that the observation confirms it is currently in place, and concluded that no decision-critical facts were missing — settling the guarding state on PRESENCE, so the §176 temporal question was never reached

WHY_THE_SECTION_176_RULE_DID_NOT_FIRE.diagnosis: placement, not wording. The §176 temporal rule lives in the established-facts list inside clarification step 2. The failing path closed the fact before reaching it, so a correct rule was never consulted.
WHY_THE_SECTION_176_RULE_DID_NOT_FIRE.consequenceForThisRepair: placement is part of the hypothesis. A property rule inserted only where §176 sits would repeat the §176 outcome — passing static proofs and changing nothing on the failing path.

INSERTION_1.name: WHICH PROPERTY THE DECISION NEEDS
INSERTION_1.location: the HEAD of `WHAT COUNTS AS ESTABLISHED`, inside clarification step 2, immediately BEFORE the pre-existing `A fact is ESTABLISHED only if the observation ... STATES it` rule and its particulars
INSERTION_1.whyThere: this is the determination of whether a fact is established. Placing the property comparison at its head makes the comparison part of that determination rather than a check applied after it. The §177 failure was a fact closed at the moment of establishment on the wrong property; the rule now sits at that moment.
content: establishment is declared property-relative: a fact is never established in the abstract, it is established FOR A PROPERTY
evidence about one property is declared SILENT about another — neither establishing nor ruling it out

five ordered steps: (i) name the owed decision and its fact; (ii) name the property the decision depends on; (iii) name the property the evidence establishes; (iv) compare — SAME PROPERTY means established, say so and move on with no hedge and no question; DIFFERENT PROPERTY means unresolved unless something else states it, and look for that something else first; (v) only then does timing arise
step (v) hands off explicitly to the §176 verification-time rule, so property is settled before moment

INSERTION_2.name: the SECOND qualification in CURRENT STATE, NOT HISTORICAL STATE
INSERTION_2.promptLines: 9 net (12 written, 3 of the 6 pre-existing §176 lines rewrapped)
INSERTION_2.location: inside `CURRENT STATE, NOT HISTORICAL STATE`, beside §176's temporal qualification of the already-answered rule
INSERTION_2.whyThere: that section is explicitly read BEFORE lists 1 and 2 and can close a fact on its own — `never ask a question the observation already answered`. It is the earlier premature-closure surface. Putting the rule only in the established-facts list would leave this path uncovered, which is exactly the §176 mistake.
content: the lead sentence moves from `One qualification, and only this one` to `Two qualifications, and only these two`, keeping the closed enumeration
a stated fact answers the question for the PROPERTY it states and says nothing either way about a different property of the same thing
the working of both qualifications is deferred to WHAT COUNTS AS ESTABLISHED, so the rule is stated once and applied once
neither qualification licenses reopening a fact whose property AND moment both match what the decision needs

WHAT_WAS_DELIBERATELY_NOT_TOUCHED.aHazardRelevantFactSection: the `treat a stated step as done` rule in `A HAZARD-RELEVANT FACT IS NOT YET A CURRENT HAZARD` is unchanged. It governs doubting whether a stated step happened, which this repair does not question — the §177 failure accepted that the verification happened and misread what it established. Editing it would have weakened a precision brake for no diagnosed reason.
WHAT_WAS_DELIBERATELY_NOT_TOUCHED.assertedConditionStateReasoning: the hazard-state path that produced the CONTROLLED candidate was left alone. Extending the property rule there would push toward `presence never establishes safety`, which the authorization forbids and which no evidence supports.
WHAT_WAS_DELIBERATELY_NOT_TOUCHED.everythingElse: schema, normalizer, verifier-v3, arbitration, authority merge, runtime routing, persistence, scorer and thresholds are untouched; proof I.5 pins five module hashes.

ORDERING_THE_PROMPT_NOW_EXPRESSES: 1. identify the owed decision-critical fact — insertion 1 step (i)
2. identify the specific property that fact requires — step (ii)
3. identify the property the supplied evidence establishes — step (iii)
5. only then mark the owed fact established or unresolved — step (iv) outcome
6. apply temporal sufficiency where time scope matters — step (v), handing off to the §176 rule
7. apply the counterfactual/decision-critical test before asking — the pre-existing five-part test, unchanged
THE_CHANGE.orderingConflict: NONE. `WHAT COUNTS AS ESTABLISHED` already declares itself as running BEFORE the five-part test, and the current-state section already carried one qualification of exactly this shape, so a second parallel qualification is expressible without contradicting any existing rule. No downstream layering was required and the STOP condition was not reached.

PRECISION_BOUNDARY_HELD.ruleCutsBothWays: the text states that a functional test establishes function completely and is itself silent about a configuration, a scope or a securement the decision may separately need — so this is not an anti-presence rule
PRECISION_BOUNDARY_HELD.presenceStillSettlesPresence: where the decision turns on presence, a stated presence establishes it COMPLETELY and asking further is named as re-litigating a stated fact
PRECISION_BOUNDARY_HELD.noQuestionInflation: a property mismatch is declared a reason a fact is unsettled and explicitly NOT permission to ask; the unresolved property must be one the current decision turns on, and the question must still pass all five parts of the counterfactual test on its own
preservedIntact: the §176 displaced-valid-fact precision brake (adjacent concerns do not inherit urgency; they go to candidates and become questions only by passing the full test on their own decision)
the burden sitting on asking, never on staying silent

CLAIM_BOUNDARY.why: every proof here reads text. Static and local success shows the rule is present, ordered, placed where the failing path runs, braked and free of row leakage. It cannot show the model behaves differently — §176 passed 30+ static proofs and changed nothing on the target row, which is the whole reason this section exists.

REMAINING_UNCERTAINTY: whether the rule fires on the failing path is unknown. Placement was chosen from the §177 raw reasoning, which shows where the model closed the fact — but a model may still close a fact without working the steps in front of it.
the hypothesis itself rests on n = 1 row across two single-sample runs on one model, and remains a hypothesis rather than an established defect.

a recall repair can cost precision. The §177 5/5 silence precision is itself uncertain (one row differing between single samples), so the precision baseline this repair must not regress is not firmly located.
